([[Hillside, New Jersey]]) | college = [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] (2018–2021) | draftyear = 2021 | career_start = 2014 | years1 = 2014–2016 | team1 = [[Basket Flames]] | years2 = 2016–2017 | team2 = [[Klosterneuburg Dukes]] | years3 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team3 = [[Grand Rapids Gold]] | years4 = 2022 | team4 = [[Guelph Nighthawks]] | years5 = [[2022-23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team5 = [[College Park Skyhawks]] | years6 = 2023 | team6 = [[Vancouver Bandits]] | years7 = 2023–2024 | team7 = [[Formosa Dreamers]] | years8 = [[2023-24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team8 = [[Iowa Wolves]] | years9 = 2024–2025 | team9 = [[BCM Gravelines-Dunkerque]] | years10 = 2025 | team10 = [[Fundación CB Granada|Covirán Granada]] | years11 = 2025 | team11 = [[AEK Larnaca B.C.]] | years12 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025-2026]] | team12 = [[Windy City Bulls]] | years13 = 2026-present | team13 = [[Satria Muda Bandung]] | highlights = }} '''Giorgi Bezhanishvili''' (born 16 November 1998) is an Austrian-Georgian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Satria Muda Bandung]] of the [[Indonesian Basketball League]] (IBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]]. ==Early life== Bezhanishvili was born in [[Rustavi]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] on 16 November 1998. In 2002, Bezhanishvili's mother Lali emigrated to [[Vienna]], [[Austria]] by way of [[Prague]], [[Czech Republic]] in search of work due to economic hardships in Georgia that resulted from the [[dissolution of the Soviet Union]]. As a result, when Bezhanishvili was 3 he and his older brother Davit moved in with their grandparents.{{cite web | url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-illinois-giorgi-bezhanishvili-mother-dancing-20181226-story.html | title='My mom is my hero': How Illini freshman Giorgi Bezhanishvili danced his way through adversity, growing up in the former Soviet republic of Georgia | publisher=[[Chicago Tribune]] | date=26 December 2018 | accessdate=17 January 2019 | author=Ryan, Shannon}} As a child, Bezhanishvili's hobbies included basketball and dancing. At the age of 10, he placed second in classical dance in a national competition. When he was 14, Bezhanishvili moved to Vienna to be with his mother.{{cite web | url=https://www.sj-r.com/sports/20181201/illini-leaning-on-overseas-freshman-giorgi-bezhanishvili | title=Illini leaning on overseas freshman Giorgi Bezhanishvili | publisher=[[The State Journal-Register]] | date=1 December 2018 | accessdate=17 January 2019 | author=Gasick, Mike}} In 2016, Bezhanishvili became a naturalized citizen of Austria.{{cite web |url=https://www.tt.com/sport/sportreport/14187145/giorgi-bezhanishvili-hat-sich-fuer-illinois-entschieden |title=Giorgi Bezhanishvili hat sich für Illinois entschieden |date=29 March 2018 |accessdate=17 January 2019 |publisher=[[Tiroler Tageszeitung]] |language=German |trans-title=Giorgi Bezhanishvili has opted for Illinois}} Bezhanishvili has learned to speak [[English language|English]], [[Georgian language|Georgian]], [[German language|German]], and [[Russian language|Russian]]. ==Youth career== After moving to Vienna, Bezhanishvili played in the youth system for the [[Basket Flames]]. From 2014 to 2016 he played for the men's senior Basket Flames team that competes in the [[2. Österreichische Basketball Bundesliga]] which is the second tier of basketball in Austria.{{cite web |url=https://www.krone.at/1680301 |title=Giorgi Bezhanishvili auf Jakob Pöltls Spuren |date=29 March 2018 |accessdate=17 January 2019 |publisher=[[Kronen Zeitung]] |language=German |trans-title=Giorgi Bezhanishvili on Jakob Pöltl's footsteps}} During the 2016–2017 season, Bezhanishvili played for the [[Klosterneuburg Dukes]] of the [[Austrian Basketball League]] and was teammates with former [[Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball|Lehigh]] player [[Michael Ojo (basketball, born 1989)|Michael Ojo]]. Ojo got Bezhanishvili connected with American basketball coaches which resulted in a scholarship to attend [[The Patrick School]] in [[Elizabeth, New Jersey]]. With Klosterneuburg, Bezhanishvili averaged 6.2 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.4 assists.{{cite web | url=http://www.news-gazette.com/sports/illini-sports/mens-basketball/2018-03-02/illini-still-working-east-coast-recruiting.html | title=Illini still working east coast recruiting | publisher=[[The News-Gazette (Champaign-Urbana)|The News-Gazette]] | date=2 March 2018 | accessdate=17 January 2019 | author=Richey, Scott}} ===Recruiting=== During his senior year of high school at [[The Patrick School]], Bezhanishvili received a scholarship offer from the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|University of Illinois]] and committed to play [[college basketball]] for head coach [[Brad Underwood]] after his official visit on 26 March 2018.{{cite web | url=https://247sports.com/college/illinois/Article/Illini-add-2018-big-man-Giorgi-Bezhanishvili-116720415/ | title=Illini add 2018 big man Giorgi Bezhanishvili | publisher=[[CBS Sports]] | work=[[247Sports.com]] | date=27 March 2018 | accessdate=17 January 2019 | author=Piper, Derek}} Bezhanishvili also had considered scholarship offers from [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]], [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]], and [[St. Bonaventure Bonnies men's basketball|St. Bonaventure]]. {{College Bezhanishvili averaged 12.5 points on 54.2 percent shooting while averaging 5.2 rebounds per game. He set [[Illinois]]' freshman scoring record with 35 points against [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]]. Bezhanishvili went through a slump midway through his sophomore season in which he shot 27 percent over nine games and came off the bench behind [[Kofi Cockburn]].{{cite news |last1=Wagner |first1=Joey |title='The game finds its way back to you.' Giorgi Bezhanishvili trying to work out of slump for Illinois basketball |url=https://herald-review.com/sports/illini/the-game-finds-its-way-back-to-you-giorgi-bezhanishvili/article_e00bec4f-a332-5e3f-81fa-1976f7175510.html |accessdate=25 March 2020 |work=[[Herald & Review]] |date=26 February 2020}} He averaged 6.8 points and 4.8 rebounds per game as a sophomore.{{cite web |last1=Welser |first1=Joel |title=ILLINOIS MEN'S BASKETBALL 2020 NCAA TOURNAMENT CAPSULE |url=https://www.collegesportsmadness.com/article/18444 |website=College Sports Madness |accessdate=25 March 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 5.1 points and 2.7 rebounds per game. Following the season, Bezhanishvili declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Ryan |first1=Shannon |title=Illinois forward Giorgi Bezhanishvili says he'll enter the NBA draft: 'I'm excited to see what the future holds' |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-illinois-basketball-giorgi-bezhanishvili-nba-draft-20210408-ag4zppi4xfbk3f6c3prs4qfo5i-story.html |access-date=13 September 2021 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=8 April 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Grand Rapids Gold (2021–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Bezhanishvili joined the [[Denver Nuggets]] for NBA Summer League play.{{cite news|title=Nuggets' Giorgi Bezhanishvili: Will play in Summer League|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nuggets-giorgi-bezhanishvili-will-play-in-summer-league/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=30 July 2021|access-date=13 September 2021}} On 13 September 2021, he signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the Nuggets.{{cite news|title=Nuggets' Giorgi Bezhanishvili: Gets camp look from Denver|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/nuggets-giorgi-bezhanishvili-gets-camp-look-from-denver/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=13 September 2021|access-date=11 October 2021}} Bezhanishvili joined the [[Grand Rapids Gold]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|title=Grand Rapids Gold Announce 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://grandrapids.gleague.nba.com/news/grand-rapids-gold-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=28 October 2021|access-date=29 October 2021}} ===College Park Skyhawks (2022–2023)=== On 25 August 2022, Bezhanishvili was traded to the [[College Park Skyhawks]].{{cite web|title=G League transactions|url= https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/transactions|website=RealGM.com|access-date=25 August 2022}} ===Vancouver Bandits (2023)=== On 28 March 2023, Bezhanishvili signed with the [[Vancouver Bandits]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].{{cite web|title=Vancouver Bandits Sign Giorgi Bezhanishvili for 2023 CEBL Season|url=https://www.cebl.ca/vancouver-bandits-sign-giorgi-bezhanishvili-for-2023-cebl-season|website=CEBL.com|date=28 March 2023|access-date=7 April 2023}} ===Formosa Dreamers (2023–2024)=== On 30 August 2023, Bezhanishvili signed with the [[Formosa Dreamers]] of the [[P. League+]].{{cite web |title=夢想家版「字母哥」 混血長人貝札尼什維利加盟 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/2571625 |publisher=ETtoday |access-date=7 September 2024 |date=30 August 2024}} On 2 January 2024, Formosa Dreamers terminated contract with Bezhanishvili.{{cite web |title=夢想家掰了206公分長人 週末回主場拚最長連勝紀錄 |url=https://sports.ltn.com.tw/news/breakingnews/4539206 |publisher=自由時報 |access-date=7 September 2024 |date=2 January 2024}} ===Iowa Wolves (2024)=== On 10 January 2024, Bezhanishvili joined the [[Iowa Wolves]] of the [[NBA G League]],{{cite web|title=Wolves Acquire Bezhanishvili From Spurs|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-acquire-bezhanishvili-from-spurs|website=NBA.com|date=10 January 2024|access-date=12 January 2024}} but was waived on 9 February.{{cite web|title=2023-24 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/2023-24-nba-g-league-transactions|website=NBA.com|access-date=23 February 2024}} On 22 February, he rejoined the Wolves. ===BCM Gravelines-Dunkerque (2024–2025)=== On 5 September 2024, Bezhanishvili signed with [[BCM Gravelines-Dunkerque]] of the [[LNB Élite]].{{cite web|title=Giorgi Bezhanishvili pour boucler le recrutement|url=http://www.bcmbasket.com/giorgi-bezhanishvili-pour-boucler-le-recrutement/|website=BCMBasket.com|date=5 September 2024|access-date=5 September 2024|language=French}} ===Covirán Granada (2025)=== On 9 March 2025, Bezhanishvili signed with [[Fundación CB Granada|Covirán Granada]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{cite web |title=Giorgi Bezhanishvili, al Coviran |url=https://www.acb.com/articulo/ver/501627-giorgi-bezhanishvili-nuevo-jugador-del-coviran-granada.html |website=ACB.COM |access-date=30 March 2025 |date=9 March 2025}} ===Windy City Bulls (2025-2026)=== Bezhanishvili played the 2025–2026 season with the [[Windy_City_Bulls|Windy City Bulls]], the [[NBA G League|NBA G-League]] affiliate of the [[Chicago Bulls]]. He played in all 36 games, starting 29 of them, and finishing the season playing an average of 31.1 minutes, 13.8 points, and 7.3 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Giorgi Bezhanishvili
